html:
The Jebel Akhdar War was fought from 1954 to 1959 between the sultan of Muscat and the imamate of inner Oman, which had governed the interior on its own since the Treaty of Seeb in 1920.

When oil companies began to explore the interior, Sultan Said bin Taimur moved to take it over. Imam Ghalib and his allies resisted, with backing from Saudi Arabia and Egypt, and retreated to the high plateau of the Jebel Akhdar. In 1959 British special forces scaled the mountain and ended the revolt.

The war ended the elected Ibadi imamate after a thousand years, and united Oman under the sultan. The exiled imam kept a claim at the Arab League for years afterwards.
